feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong senior digital/public-sector CV with clear positioning, credible progression, and relevant platform/communications leadership. It reads professionally and is mostly polished, but it is somewhat dense and repetitive, with a few style inconsistencies and opportunities to sharpen impact through clearer outcomes.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear leadership narrative: strong progression at NACo into director-level ownership of web, analytics, governance, and multimedia.  
- Good credibility signals: scale metrics (10,000+ pages, 3.5M annual page views, 50+ publishers) and concrete platforms/tools strengthen trust.  
- Broad but coherent skill set: strategy, CMS, analytics, AI search, and production align well with the target brand.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce repetition and tighten structure: “digital communications,” “workflows,” “governance,” and “platform” language recurs heavily across sections; consolidate Core Competencies/Topline Skills/Technical + IT to avoid overlap.  
- Add more outcome-focused evidence: several bullets describe responsibilities rather than results; include measurable improvements in engagement, efficiency, adoption, search performance, or campaign outcomes.  
- Fix minor style/grammar consistency issues: “social, and multimedia” should be “social and multimedia”; standardize serial comma usage, hyphenation (“member-facing,” “broadcast-quality”), and title casing. No major misspellings found.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong positioning and relevant scope, but it’s slightly dense and repeats language already covered in the subtitle, core competencies, and work experience. Tightening it with a clearer value proposition and a few concrete anchors will improve impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Consider: “Digital platform and communications leader with 12+ years of experience modernizing enterprise web ecosystems for public-sector and mission-driven organizations. Builds the governance, analytics, editorial, and multimedia systems that support high-volume publishing, stronger user experiences, and more effective digital operations.”
- Replace “building the platforms” with “modernizing enterprise web ecosystems” for sharper, more senior phrasing.
- Change “Leads” to “Builds” or “Delivers” to avoid a sentence fragment and create a more direct value statement.
- If space allows, add one concrete scale marker from recent roles, such as “10,000+ page website” or “3.5M annual page views.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled user experiences” overlaps with core competencies and recent projects; keep it only if AI is a target role priority.
- “Governance models,” “editorial systems,” and “analytics infrastructure” are repeated across multiple sections.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block largely repeats the header and Topline Skills. It will be more effective if tightened, made more parallel in style, and focused on differentiating strengths rather than restating broad areas.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use shorter, more scannable noun phrases with consistent structure; avoid mixing functions, sectors, and outputs in one list.
- Replace “Advocacy and public-sector communications” with a more capability-led phrase tied to leadership scope.
- Consider this rewrite: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial operations • Analytics, dashboards and reporting infrastructure • Cross-channel communications leadership • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integration • Public-sector advocacy communications • Video, livestream and multimedia production
- If space allows, prioritize the most senior/recent strengths first: web modernization, governance, analytics, AI search.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise website modernization,” “analytics infrastructure,” “editorial systems,” and “AI-enabled…experiences” closely duplicate the header.
- This section also overlaps heavily with Topline Skills; consider using one or the other as the primary skills summary.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot, but it reads dense and overlaps with work-experience bullets. Tightening phrasing and emphasizing outcomes or scope will make it more distinctive and scannable.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Add a one-line intro such as “Selected recent projects” and keep each item to one crisp, parallel sentence.
- Use consistent action/result structure: “Built/Developed X using Y to achieve Z.”
- Tighten wording: change “designed for continued campaign growth” to “built for future campaign expansion”; use “10 x 20-foot” for style consistency.
- If possible, add one concrete signal of scale or impact for 1–2 projects.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite development, and advocacy video series substantially repeat current freelance/NACo experience; reframe as named examples rather than restating duties.
- “Editorial storytelling,” “web features,” and “production and distribution” are somewhat generic; sharpen to avoid repeating broader competencies already listed elsewhere.

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with clear strategic + technical breadth, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the header, competencies, and NACo entries. Tighten it around distinctive consulting impact, named initiatives, and outcomes.

Suggested edit
- Open with scope + client type + value: “Embedded as a full-time strategic communications consultant for a U.S. national membership organization, leading web modernization, campaign delivery, and content operations improvement.”
- Replace generic verbs (“support,” “advise”) with ownership verbs: led, built, launched, redesigned, standardized, improved.
- Consolidate into 4–5 bullets focused on differentiators:
- Led Drupal-based campaign and storytelling builds, including microsites, modular content components, and downloadable member toolkits.
- Built communications workflows, analytics/reporting, and governance practices to improve cross-channel coordination across web, email, social, and multimedia.
- Delivered front-end/CMS implementation and troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Shaped an AI-enabled search initiative spanning retrieval strategy, structured content, and discovery UX.
- Add metrics if available: number of sites/pages, users, publishers, campaign launches, time saved, search success, engagement lift.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Governance,” “analytics,” and “enterprise web improvement” repeat NACo and the summary; keep only if tied to new consulting outcomes.
- The AI search and microsite work also appears in Recent Projects; avoid repeating the same detail verbatim.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with solid scale metrics. Tighten the opening, foreground the biggest outcomes, and avoid repeating channel-management points already covered in earlier NACo roles.

Suggested edit
- Replace the broad lead sentence with a sharper scope/outcome summary: “Directed NACo’s digital media function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Lead with the website modernization win and keep it results-first: “Led redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website to Drupal, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make channel leadership more specific if possible: add email open/click growth, audience growth, engagement rates, production volume, or cost/time savings from the studio build.
- Tighten the final bullets into impact language: “Built NACo’s first in-house broadcast studio…” / “Implemented GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery reporting…” / “Established governance, publishing standards, and cross-department planning workflows…”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director entry; keep this version focused on enterprise leadership and measurable scale.
- Video/programming language may overlap with Recent Projects; emphasize studio build and operational capacity here.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the later Director role and earlier Digital Media Manager role. Make it more specific to what you owned at this level: executional leadership, editorial coordination, and channel growth.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + function: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications across web, email, social and video, coordinating editorial execution for advocacy and member communications.”
- Tighten bullets around distinct contributions: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Rephrase video bullet to show ownership and outcome: “Produced and scaled a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Combine workflow/editorial bullets: “Improved cross-team editorial planning and digital publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video” is too close to the Director of Digital Media opening.
- “Weekly video updates” also appears in the 2015–2018 role; distinguish this entry as scaling/formalizing the program.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this skills block is too generic and overlaps heavily with the header and Core Competencies. Tighten it to emphasize leadership scope and public-sector relevance without repeating exact phrases used elsewhere.

Suggested edit:
- Replace broad nouns with sharper capability labels: “Enterprise digital strategy” → “Enterprise digital strategy for public-sector platforms”
- Make leadership and operating-model strength clearer: “Editorial systems and governance” → “Editorial governance, publishing standards, and content operations”
- Tighten “Multi-channel communications leadership” to “Cross-channel communications leadership” for concision
- Consider revised version:
- Enterprise digital strategy for mission-driven organizations
- Editorial governance, publishing standards, and content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy communications
- Audience-centered content strategy

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “Editorial systems and governance” duplicate both the header and Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Audience-focused content planning” is weaker and less distinctive than the operational strengths shown in recent roles.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads like a raw tool list and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize higher-value platform leadership and current strengths, not repeat every technology.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools to capability clusters: “Drupal and enterprise CMS platforms • CMS modernization and migration • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based operational systems • AI-enabled search and discovery”
- Drop lower-signal or older items unless central to target roles; consider removing “jQuery” and possibly “WordPress/SharePoint/Power Pages” if they are not recent differentiators.
- Put the strongest, most current items first: Drupal, CMS modernization, AI-enabled search, integrations/automation.
- If keeping multiple platforms, group them: “Enterprise CMS platforms: Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially duplicates “Technical + IT”; keep Topline Skills broader and reserve detailed tool names for the technical section.
- “AI-enabled search experiences” also appears in Core Competencies, so avoid repeating the exact phrasing.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster for a senior digital leader, but it reads as a tool list rather than a value statement. It also overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” analytics section, so this version should emphasize strategic application over software names.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-first to outcomes-first, e.g. “Analytics strategy, reporting & optimization” rather than a pure platform list.
- Tighten and group related items: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity” + “KPI framework design, executive reporting, SEO/performance analysis.”
- Consider stronger phrasing: replace “Leadership reporting” with “Executive dashboarding and decision support.”
- Optional rewrite: “Analytics infrastructure (GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity) • KPI and measurement framework design • Executive dashboarding and reporting • SEO and digital performance analysis”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates the “Data, Analytics & Optimization” section in Technical + IT almost exactly.
- Since recent experience already proves these tools in the NACo role, use this topline item to signal strategic analytics leadership, not repeat the stack.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This skill block is relevant, but it reads generic and overlaps with both Core Competencies and multiple NACo bullets. Tighten it to emphasize higher-value, recent capabilities and use sharper phrasing.

Suggested edit:
- Replace broad terms with more senior, outcome-oriented wording: “Broadcast-quality video production,” “Livestream and hybrid event delivery,” “PTZ camera and studio systems,” “Virtual event operations.”
- Consider a tighter version: “Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • PTZ camera and studio systems • Studio operations and run-of-show execution”
- If accurate, add scale or complexity in adjacent experience bullets instead of here, e.g., audience size, event frequency, or in-house studio buildout.
- Drop “editing” unless post-production is a meaningful differentiator; “video production” already implies it.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Multimedia production and livestream operations” already appears in Core Competencies; avoid repeating the same phrasing.
- “Hybrid and virtual event production” overlaps with NACo studio/event bullets, so keep this skills line concise rather than descriptive.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it reads as a generic inventory and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. This item should either be tightened to emphasize strongest/recent CMS expertise or differentiated by proficiency/context.

Suggested edit:
- Prioritize most relevant platforms first and group by depth: “Drupal (enterprise, migration, microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint / Power Pages • GitHub Pages”
- If space allows, add a light qualifier to show level, not just names: “Enterprise CMS: Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages; Static publishing: GitHub Pages”
- Consider dropping GitHub Pages unless it supports a meaningful project; it feels less central than the enterprise platforms in recent roles.
- Keep wording aligned with recent experience, especially Drupal, which is clearly the strongest and most evidenced platform.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates Topline Skills [2]; consider merging or making this section more tool-focused while Topline Skills stays strategic.
- “CMS modernization” already appears elsewhere, so avoid repeating that phrase here unless adding platform-specific evidence.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical coverage, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” Tighten it to emphasize implementation tools not already captured elsewhere and use cleaner, more current phrasing.

Suggested edit:
- Rename/refocus to: **Front-End & Technical Implementation**
- Replace with: **HTML/CSS • JavaScript/jQuery • REST/API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions (CI/CD)**
- Drop version numbers unless required; **HTML5/CSS3** adds little value and dates the section.
- If accurate, consider adding one stronger modern qualifier tied to recent work, e.g. **Drupal front-end implementation**, **CMS troubleshooting**, or **deployment automation**.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- **HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery** already appears under Topline Skills; keep it in one place or vary the framing.
- **API integrations** and broader technical execution also overlap with Core Competencies and recent freelance bullets; avoid repeating identical wording.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow systems leadership. It should emphasize automation/building systems, not just collaboration apps, especially given the stronger recent experience in governance and cross-team operations.

Suggested edit:
- Split “automation” tools from “project/collaboration” tools to improve signal: “Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier” and “Jira • Asana • Trello • Basecamp.”
- Remove lower-value chat tools unless they are central to workflow design: Slack and Teams are too generic for this category.
- Consider renaming to “Workflow Automation & Operations Systems” to align with the core competency language.
- If space allows, add a light qualifier for impact: “Airtable systems • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira/Asana/Trello workflow management.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable systems” and “Workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating the exact phrasing here.
- Jira, Asana, Basecamp, Trello overlap heavily; listing all four may feel padded unless each is genuinely current/relevant.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Relevant tools for your recent leadership roles, but this line is too bare and misses the scale/ownership already shown in your NACo experience. It would be stronger if framed as platforms used to run high-volume member communications.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms**
- Rewrite as: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp** only if these were hands-on systems you actively managed; otherwise remove weaker/older tools.
- If space allows, add light context: **Enterprise email and member engagement platforms for newsletters, journeys, and audience communications**
- Prioritize the platform most tied to recent work first; if Higher Logic was central at NACo, consider: **Higher Logic • Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Mailchimp**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps with repeated “email/newsletters” references in Work Experience; keep this item tool-focused, not responsibility-focused.
- If Mailchimp was minor or older, it may dilute the stronger enterprise positioning created elsewhere in the CV.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tool stack, but this item currently duplicates the “Topline Skills” analytics section almost exactly. In Technical + IT, it should read more like a concise tools/methods list and avoid broad terms already covered elsewhere.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with: **GA4 • BigQuery • Looker Studio • Power BI • Microsoft Clarity • Google Search Console • A/B testing • KPI dashboard development**
- Swap **SEO** for **Google Search Console** or **technical SEO analysis** to make the skill more concrete and tool-oriented.
- Replace **Dashboarding** with **KPI dashboard development** or **executive reporting dashboards** for sharper phrasing.
- Order by strongest/recently evidenced tools first: GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, Looker Studio, Clarity.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps heavily with **Topline Skills → Analytics, Insights & Optimization**; consider trimming one version or making this one strictly tool-based.
- “A/B testing” is not clearly evidenced in recent experience; keep only if you can support it with examples elsewhere.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is too broad and overlaps with the 2018–2024 NACo roles. Make it more foundational and execution-focused, with clearer scope and any measurable outputs.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize early-team building and hands-on production: “Promoted across two digital roles to help establish NACo’s first in-house digital media function, improving execution across web, email, social and multimedia.”
- Add concrete contributions and scale where possible: website refresh scope, number/frequency of livestreams or weekly videos, audience reach, event support, or production volume.
- Tighten the management line: replace “providing day-to-day guidance” with “mentored a digital media associate” or “supervised daily work of one associate.”
- Keep verbs distinct from later roles: use “supported,” “produced,” “implemented,” and “helped build,” not “led” or “directed.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director entry; frame this as launching or early producing the series.
- “Strengthening workflows” repeats later governance/operations themes; keep this lighter and more tactical here.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry with a credible “first podcast” achievement, but it reads generic and overlaps with later NACo digital/media roles. Emphasize the innovation/program support angle and keep the digital piece concise.

Suggested edit:
- Lead with scope and support function: “Coordinated county innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo program development and policy priorities.”
- Tighten the multimedia line and make the podcast the standout: “Produced digital and multimedia content, including launching NACo’s first podcast and leading planning, scripting, and production.”
- If possible, add outcomes: number of projects supported, podcast episodes launched, audiences reached, or internal teams/programs served.
- Consider a sharper version: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives for NACo programs and policy teams; produced digital content and launched the organization’s first podcast, leading concept development, scripting, and production.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with later digital/media roles; keep this item more focused on innovation/research support plus the podcast launch.
- Avoid repeating broad multimedia language already covered more strongly in 2015–2024 roles.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid supporting skills, but this item reads a bit dated and overlaps with stronger multimedia claims elsewhere. Tighten it to emphasize current, professional production capability rather than generic creative software.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Multimedia Production Tools**
